statements.venue: Press release on reintroducing the NO FAKES Act
statements.quote: The use of AI is only growing, and Congress must catch up with common sense, common ground regulations
statements.context: Announcing the bipartisan, bicameral NO FAKES Act, which gives people a federal right to control digital replicas of their voice and likeness, to protect against deepfakes.
statements.reason: Calls for AI regulation in the context of deepfakes and likeness rights, without acknowledging catastrophic risk.

statements.venue: Press release on introducing the TRAIN Act
statements.quote: As AI rapidly evolves and becomes more present in our lives, our laws must catch up — that includes preserving the dignity of artists and the authenticity of their work
statements.context: Announcing the bipartisan TRAIN Act, which would let creators find out whether their work was used to train AI models.
statements.reason: About copyright and transparency of AI training data, not catastrophic risk.

slowdown.note: No statement found on slowing frontier AI development.

pause.note: No statement found on pausing frontier AI development.

intl.note: No statement found on coordinating with China on the pace of AI development.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI.

record: Led the House reintroduction of the NO FAKES Act with Rep. Salazar and Senators Blackburn and Coons, creating a federal right to control digital replicas of one's voice and likeness (deepfakes).
Introduced the bipartisan TRAIN Act with Rep. Moran, letting creators learn whether their work was used to train AI models.
With Senator Klobuchar and Rep. Salazar, asked the Justice Department to investigate sexually explicit AI-generated images made with Grok.
With Senator Warren, led a letter (26 signers) asking the Commerce Department inspector general to investigate Secretary Lutnick's family's conflicts of interest in AI data center decisions.
grade_reason: Her 2026 AI work is substantial but concerns deepfakes, likeness rights, creators' copyright, explicit AI images and data center conflicts of interest; nothing found acknowledges catastrophic risk from AI.
notes: All six required web searches ran this time, plus one on Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act cosponsors (7 total).
